task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of May 1, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style reported feature about the sorting work at Morrow Cupboard thrift shop and why donated goods do not arrive as ready-made money for its education fund.

facts.text: An April 2026 stock note records Morrow Cupboard volunteers separating saleable jackets from a donation containing incomplete bedding sets and damaged clothing.
The nonprofit shop raises money for adult music-study bursaries and employs a part-time manager.
Its April intake ledger records 1,200 donated items: 740 priced for sale, 260 accepted by a recycling partner and 200 sent for disposal.
Items priced for sale had not all sold by month-end, so the 740 count is not a cash-sales total.
The shop pays rent, the manager's wages, utilities and waste-handling charges despite receiving its stock without a purchase price.
Its published annual account records an $18,000 transfer to the bursary fund after the shop's stated operating expenses.
That transfer funded six $3,000 bursaries, not a $3,000 payment to every person taking local music classes.
The record contains no measured change in recipients' eventual earnings or musical careers.
Manager Cera Veylan says condition, completeness and seasonal demand affect whether an item can be priced and displayed.
Veylan said, "The donation arrives once. We still have to sort it, find room for it and sometimes pay to take it away."
Fourteen volunteers contribute different amounts of time; the shop does not operate with fourteen full-time unpaid workers.
Volunteer Omi Nelden says evaluating an unfamiliar item can take longer than putting a familiar garment on a rack.
Nelden said, "A bag at the door is a question about what is inside, not a price tag we can already count."
The recycling partner accepts specified textiles and does not guarantee that every rejected shop item can be recycled.
The shop has begun limiting donation drop-offs to staffed hours so volunteers can explain what it currently accepts.
The change has not been evaluated for its effect on donations, disposal costs or shop income.
Customers can buy ordinary clothing without applying for financial assistance or identifying their household income.
The board is considering more storage but has not signed a lease or approved additional paid hours.
The shop occupies a former music-supply store and retains its long glass-fronted display cabinet.
No verified weight-based landfill diversion or carbon-saving estimate is supplied for the April item counts.

forbidden_additions: All 740 priced items sold, all donated goods are recyclable or donated stock has no handling costs
Fourteen full-time volunteers, universal bursaries or a verified carbon-saving calculation
